Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Intro + quick demo? (time options)

Hi Rishi / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. Ravi and I would love a 30–45 min demo of Redwood Inference next week to show our cloud and platform teams. I put up a Doodle poll with a few windows (I selected generic "10:00" options to keep it simple) but I realized afterwards that Doodle may be converting times to my browser locale (I'm currently in Berlin/CET).

Participants: Amanda (Berlin/CET), Ravi (Bangalore/IST), and our Head of Platform (San Francisco/PT). That mix makes me nervous about all the implicit conversions. Can you confirm whether you prefer we:
- 1) pick an explicit UTC slot (my preference), or
- 2) pick a labeled US time (e.g., 9:00 PT / 12:00 ET) and you send ICS?

Doodle poll: https://doodle.com/poll/abc123-finpulse-demo (screenshot attached)

Attaching a screenshot of the poll — seems some slots showed up as 10:00 CET in my browser, which isn't what the SF folks saw.

Thanks,
Amanda

--
Amanda Siegel
Head of Integrations, FinPulse
amanda.siegel@finpulse.com
FinPulse, London / Berlin

Amanda — thanks for flagging this. Short answer: we prefer sending a single confirmed event in UTC (and include common local equivalents) to avoid browser/localization ambiguity.

Quick proposal to keep things simple: please pick one of these explicit UTC slots and we'll send a calendar invite with ICS (UTC + common conversions in the description).

- Option A: 2027-05-20 16:00 UTC (9:00 PT / 12:00 ET / 17:00 CET / 21:30 IST) — 45 min
- Option B: 2027-05-21 14:00 UTC (7:00 PT / 10:00 ET / 15:00 CET / 19:30 IST) — 30 min

Notes:
- US DST is in effect (so PT/ET offsets are DST-aware); Europe is on summer time (CET/CEST) so labeling as "CEST (UTC+2)" can be ambiguous in some tools — I’ll write the label as "CEST (UTC+2)" if we send an invite.
- India does not observe DST (IST = UTC+5:30) so we'll state the .5 offset explicitly.

If you confirm one option and which stakeholders must attend (Ravi + Platform lead?), we'll send ICS in UTC and also attach a multi-timezone ICS for the FinPulse attendees.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

In the past some team members' Outlook clients interpreted ICS DTSTART in local time and shifted the event.

Attaching confirmation screenshot from our side.

Amanda / team — great, Option A confirmed on our side. I created two ICS files: one where DTSTART/DTEND are explicit UTC timestamps (redwood-demo-utc.ics) and another that contains separate VEVENTs for common local times (redwood-demo-multitz.ics).

We will send the official invite with the UTC ICS; the invite description will list:
- 2027-05-20 16:00 UTC
- 2027-05-20 09:00 PT (San Francisco) — PDT (UTC-7)
- 2027-05-20 12:00 ET (New York) — EDT (UTC-4)
- 2027-05-20 18:00 CEST (Berlin) — CEST (UTC+2)
- 2027-05-20 21:30 IST (Bangalore) — IST (UTC+5:30)

A couple small pieces of context so everyone's calendar behaves:
- We've set the ICS DTSTART/DTEND as UTC (Z suffix) to avoid client-level local conversions.
- For Outlook users who've historically had import issues, the multi-timezone ICS is a fallback (import the second file).
- We'll include a one-line note about DST: "Dates are expressed in UTC; local offsets shown are for clarity and reflect DST/ summer time where applicable."

I'll send the official invite from events@redwood.com shortly — you should get an email with the UTC ICS and the multi-timezone fallback.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

—Marissa
